I have been farming the land in Quzhou for more than forty years. I never went to school, but I learned everything by working the fields with my husband and watching what the neighbors do. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — that is what the soil and the wells are good for. I have about twelve mu of land. I will plant wheat on ten mu this autumn, and after we cut it in early June, I will put maize straight into the same fields without ploughing again. I will also keep two mu for cotton because the cotton price has been steady and I need the cash for medicine and daily expenses. For the wheat, I will rotary till the soil like I always do, sow the improved wheat seeds that my neighbor used last year, and spread about twenty jin of nitrogen fertilizer per mu — I would rather put a little too much than risk a thin harvest. I will irrigate four times from the well: winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and filling. For maize, I will use no-tillage and plant the hybrid denghai605 seeds because they grow fast and yield well. I will give the maize two irrigations and spray for insects and weeds two or three times. The cotton needs more spraying — about fourteen times — but the money is worth it. I do not use much pure phosphorus or potassium by themselves, but the compound fertilizer I buy has some in it, so I figure the wheat gets about twelve jin of phosphorus and four jin of potassium per mu, the maize gets less, and the cotton gets a bit more of everything to keep the bolls growing.
